chief_complaint: right lower quadrant abdominal pain and fever
hpi_details: 45M presents with 12 hours of periumbilical pain that has now migrated to the right lower quadrant, accompanied by nausea, one episode of vomiting, and subjective fever.
expectations: wants pain relief and a CT scan

investigation_events.title: Urgent appendicitis results
investigation_events.availability_message: The urgent appendicitis results are now available; IV fluids, analgesia, antibiotics, and surgical consultation should not be delayed.

results.test: CT abdomen and pelvis with IV contrast
results.value: Dilated appendix measuring 10 mm with periappendiceal fat stranding; no abscess, perforation, or free air

core_concepts: Classic presentation is periumbilical pain migrating to RLQ.
Diagnosis is often confirmed with CT scan in adults.
common_misconceptions: Assuming all RLQ pain is appendicitis.
dangerous_errors: Discharging patient with classic migrating pain without imaging or observation.
management_principles: NPO, IV fluids, analgesia, antibiotics, surgery consultation.

source_refs.title: SAGES & ACS Evidence-Based Surgical Practice Guidelines

reference_soap.subjective: 45M with migrating RLQ pain, nausea, and fever.
reference_soap.objective: T 38.2C, RLQ tenderness with guarding (McBurney's point).
reference_soap.plan: CT abdomen/pelvis, NPO, IV fluids, surgery consult.

teaching.one_liner: Classic acute appendicitis presenting with migrating RLQ pain, fever, and nausea.

must_ask.say: Did the pain start around your belly button and then move to your lower right side?
When exactly did the pain start, and how has it changed since then?
Have you lost your appetite, felt nauseated, or vomited?
Have you had any fever or chills?
Does moving, coughing, or pressing on your belly make the pain worse?
